answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, time-locked stake: it must lock tokens before a pulse of proposals, and rewards accrue only after a glacier-long delay if independent reviewers confirm useful work. Splitting one identity into a vine of fresh accounts does not multiply influence, because every account needs its own locked stake and each earns only a capped share. A sybil attacker therefore ties up more capital for longer, risks losing it to slashing, and must still produce work that survives review.
